19. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and arguments, I answer the above issues in all 3 cases as follows: -
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative,,
 Issue No.3: As per final order for the  following;
 REASONS 20. ISSUE NO.1 IN ALL 3 CASES: It is the case of petitioners that, they sustained injuries in the road traffic accident which occurred on 31.08.2024 due to alleged rash and negligent driving of driver of Maxi Cab bearing no.KA-51-AH-7921.
To prove this fact mother of minor petitioner in MVC 7897/2024 got examined as P.W.1 and petitioner in MVC No.7898/2024 as P.W.2 and Petitioner in MVC No 7899/2024 is examined as P.W.3.

22. On the basis of this first information, Kumarswamy police registered Crime No.148/2024 against T.T driver by name Basavaraj and 2 wheeler rider by name Mohammad Rehan, who is petitioner in MVC No.7898/2024.
For tripple riding against the bike rider and for negligence against T.T driver.
On the next day of the accident, spot panchanama is conducted which shows the spot of the accident is Gottigere main road and there is divider in between the road 50ft wide road.
As per the spot sketch accident has taken place in the middle of the road.
Admittedly, the petitioners were tripple riding, one of them was minor.
Both the vehicles got damaged as per IMV report.
Front left side bumper of T.T and left side crash guard and rear view mirror of bike got damaged.
As per the wound certificate (SCCH-12) 14 MVC. No.7897,7898 & 7899/2024 petitioner Vijaya Raghavan sustained one grievous injury left Recon eye and simple injury of abrasion to left hand, knee.

After investigation charge sheet is filed against both the vehicle drivers stating that, T.T driver was negligent in riding the T.T and bike rider was riding with 2 pillion riders and there was no D.L to him.

The bike owner gave the vehicle to person having no D.L as such charge sheet is filed against bike rider, bike owner and T.T driver.
23.
In the cross examination of P.W.1, he denied negligence on part of bike rider and attributed negligence to T.T driver.
The authorized representative of insurance company deposed vice- versa and denied negligence on part of T.T driver and attributed negligence to bike rider.

On perusal of IMV report, spot sketch, spot mahazar and final report it can be noticed that accident has taken place in the middle of the road and the contention of petitioner that, bike rider was riding the vehicle by observing traffic rules cannot be believed.

The bike rider with the knowledge that tripple riding is not permitted, took the minor also on two wheeler and there are all chances that due to heavy weight, he may not be able to control the vehicle.
Therefore, attributing entire negligence to T.T driver is not proper.
Petitioner bike rider having violated several traffic rules
is not only accused as per charge sheet, but also negligent in riding the bike in the opinion of this court.

In that view of the matter, I am of the opinion that bike rider has contributed to the accident to the extent of 50%
and negligence on part of the T.T driver is (SCCH-12) 15 MVC. No.7897,7898 & 7899/2024 remaining 50%.
Accordingly this issue in all 3 cases is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
24. ISSUE NO.2 IN MVC No.7897/2024:
To prove the age of minor petitioner, PW-1 has produced Aadhaar card at Ex.P.11 which shows that his date of birth is 01.07.2008.
Accident took place on 31.08.2024.
He was aged 16 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 16 years at the time of accident.
25. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was coolie, but no documents are produced to that effect.
He being minor, it cannot be said that he was doing any avocation.

Therefore, there is no avocation or earning of income by the petitioner but, even in the case of accident to minor,
compensation has to be worked out in non pecuniary heads, including treatment, transportation,
attendant charges, pain and suffering and loss of amenities of life.

It is observed that, appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to actual expenditure towards treatment, attendant etc should be if disability is above 10% to 30% of the whole body Rs.3,00,000/-, upto 60% Rs.4,00,000/- upto 90%
Rs.5,00,000/- and above 90% it shall be (SCCH-12) 16 MVC. No.7897,7898 & 7899/2024 Rs.6,00,000/- and upto 10% it should be Rs.1,00,000/- unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
To prove permanent disability petitioner not got examined any doctor.
Therefore, there is no functional disability affecting the income of petitioner.
26. In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of T.T bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AH-7921 and his 50% negligence is proved in the accident.
Hence petitioner is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained injuries to left recon eye and minor abrasion, out of which injury to eye is said to be grievous in nature.

Therefore,
for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- .
(ii) For Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12.
They show that he has paid Rs.34,418/- as medical expenses.
Those bills are disputed by the respondents, but nothing worthwhile is brought out to disbelieve the bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.34,418/- .
(iii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was in hospital for 03 days a per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.09.
Accident took place in the year 2024.
Hence, food and nourishment charges of Rs.500/- x 03 days = Rs.1,500/-is awarded.
(SCCH-12) 17 MVC. No.7897,7898 & 7899/2024 (iv) For Attendant charges: For a period of inpatient for 03 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Hence, attendant charges Rs.500/- x 03 days =Rs.1,500/-is awarded.
(v) For Loss of income during laid up period: As there is no income can be considered for minor, no compensation is awarded for loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted from spot of accident to the hospital.
He spent money for traveling to hospital.
Considering those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.2,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
(vii) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the aforesaid finding, there is no functional disability to the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

(viii) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :
As there is no evidence of doctor, it is not possible to assess how injury caused to petitioner has affected his life.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(ix) For Future medical expenses: There is no evidence regarding need of future medical treatment to petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(x) For loss of future prospects:
Even in injury cases, court has to consider whether future prospect is affected by the accidental injuries to victim.
In this case, on considering the oral and documentary evidence no such loss of future prospect is evident in respect of petitioner.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for (SCCH-12) 18 MVC.
